paper.title: Meritocratic Fairness via $K$-Shapley Values in Budgeted Combinatorial Bandits with Full-Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Budgeted Combinatorial MAB with full-bandit feedback (BCMAB-FBF), meritocratic fairness via K-Shapley values
unmapped: Objective is query-normalized meritocratic fairness regret: L1 distance between the learner's arm-marginal vector and the K-Shapley-proportional policy pi*(i)=K phi_i^K / sum_j phi_j^K, not reward regret
Set valuation V is a general monotone set function on sets of size <= K with V(empty)=0 (not necessarily linear)
Assumes optimal fair policy pi* lies in S_{M,K} (no coordinate exceeds 1)
IW-KSVFair: the learner knows a lower bound epsilon on the K-Shapley values
settings.definition_quote: In a Budgeted Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandit with full bandit feedback (BCMAB-FBF), at each time step $t$, the learner selects a subset of arms $S_t$ with $|S_t| \le K$ from a finite set of arms $[M] = \{1,2,\dots,M\}$ and receives a stochastic reward $V_t(S_t)$. ... For each $S \in \mathcal{A}$, let $D_S$ denote a fixed but unknown reward distribution supported on $[0,1]$ with mean $V(S)$.

bound.regime: fixed M, K with 1 < K < M

conditions: 1 < m < K (paper: 1 < K < M), M and K fixed
valuation monotone submodular with phi_i^K >= epsilon for all arms

source.label: thm:k2-fairness-lower-bound
source.quote: Consider BCMAB-FBF with fixed $M$ and $K$ with $1 < K < M$. Then, there exists a monotone  submodular valuation function satisfying $\epsilon \le \phi_i^K\ \forall i\in [M]$ such that, for every algorithm, $   \text{sup}_V \mathrm{FR}_T(V) = \Omega(T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Quantity is query-normalized fairness regret. Paper's M = canonical K (base arms), paper's K = canonical m (budget). Proof constant min{c1, alpha/(2 binom(M-1,K-1))}.

symbols.gamma: lower bound on the sum of K-Shapley values, sum_a phi_a^K >= gamma > 0

tuning: R = Theta_tilde(T^{2/3}) exploration samples per arm

source.label: thm:muras
source.quote: Assume that for every arm $a\in[M]$, the $K$-Shapley value satisfies $\phi_a^K\in[0,1]$, and let $\sum_{a=1}^M \phi_a^K\ge \gamma>0$. Then, with $R=\tilde \Theta(T^{2/3})$ the cumulative fairness regret satisfies $\mathrm{FR}_T = \tilde O\left(\frac{KM}{\gamma}T^{2/3}\right)$.

results.notes: Paper's KM = m*K canonical (symmetric). Fairness regret, quantity other.

symbols.C_proj: C = max_t max{1, ||tilde pi_t||_inf} <= K (paper's K = budget m)
symbols.eps_phi: lower bound epsilon on all K-Shapley values, phi_a^K in [epsilon,1]

conditions: distribution P_t over K-sets with marginals pi_t is exactly computable

source.quote: Assume that the $K$-Shapley values satisfy $\phi_a^K \in [\epsilon,1]$ for all $a\in[M]$. Assume that at each round $t$, the distribution $P_t$ over $K$-sets is exactly computable with marginals $\pi_t$. Then, for $\eta = \Theta(\frac{M^{2/3}}{K^{1/3}T^{1/3}} )$, the expected cumulative fairness regret of \ouralgo\ satisfies \[ \mathrm{FR}_T = \widetilde{O}\left( \frac{C}{\epsilon}K^{2/3} M^{2/3} T^{2/3} + \frac{C}{\epsilon}M^{4/3}K^{1/3}T^{1/3} \right). \] Here, $C = \max_t c_t$ with $c_t = \max\{1,||\tilde{\pi}_t||_\infty\}\le K$.

results.notes: Paper's M -> canonical K, paper's K -> canonical m. Exact P_t requires enumeration over binom(M,K) sets, so compute not stated as polynomial.
